source_text: Penile cancer, though rare (global incidence ~1 per 100,000 males annually), shows a strong association with retained foreskin, with meta-analyses indicating odds ratios as low as 0.33 for invasive disease in those circumcised early in life, linked to chronic inflammation, HPV persistence, and poor hygiene in the subpreputial area. [84] [85]
